items.title: bug: [iOS] Push still reports enabled after system notification permission is revoked
items.body:
### heca version

0.1.0-nightly-20260918-1

### Surface

Mobile app (iOS)

### Agent provider (if relevant)

Not provider-related

### Steps to reproduce

Precondition: Heca is paired, iOS initially allows Heca notifications, and a Relay push subscription already exists.

1. Open Heca Settings → Notifications and enable push; observe the enabled status.
2. In iOS Settings → Notifications → Heca App, turn off Allow Notifications.
3. Return to Heca's Notifications page and inspect the status.
4. Turn the existing Relay push subscription off, then on again.

### Expected behavior

Show the server subscription state separately from this iPhone's current OS permission. With permission denied, show an actionable warning and a way to restore permission in Settings. Keeping the subscription active may be valid, but its status must not imply that this phone can display notifications.

### Actual behavior

Heca still says `推送已启用` (Push enabled) after OS permission is disabled. Turning the existing subscription off and on produces the same green success message, with no permission warning or recovery guidance.

### How often does it happen?

Sometimes — observed both on returning to the page and after re-enabling the existing subscription in this sequence; no wider frequency was measured.

### Logs / screenshots

Sequential captures: iOS Allow Notifications is Off; the later Heca capture shows enabled status and a green success message. These are different steps, not a simultaneous screen.

![iOS permission Off and subsequent Heca enabled status](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/wanghuan-520/74236d906094bbfd42780c8a8cb2ddcb/raw/541caeaa799985d564310ac90a23d5cce1ede02f/01-permission-state.svg)

Screenshots are cropped and annotated copies. Private host/session identifiers, account context and paths have been removed or opaquely redacted; source metadata has been stripped. Numbered boxes and explanatory text are added annotations. Original UI text and control states have not been rewritten. Unredacted originals remain local.

### Additional context

Confirmed permission/status feedback issue, tested through a real iPhone using iPhone Mirroring. This does not establish an APNs-wide delivery failure and does not cover first registration without a token.

Source lead: `notifications_tab.dart` uses the existing subscription's `active` flag in `_enabledRowSubtitle`; the existing-subscription branch of `_setEnabled` calls `pushUpdate` without rechecking OS permission there. Read-only source review used the matching 0.1.0-nightly-20260918-1 tag, commit `fe82b65e7fc2d5e9dbf65fd4e7137a9f41612078`. The paired daemon revision was not independently verified.

Local tracking ID: `IOS-PG33-PERMISSION-STATE-20260921`. Published from existing test records on 2026-09-21; preparing this report did not trigger additional model requests.

items.title: Per-image mutation routes authorize and write in separate statements, so a revoked permission still applies
items.body:
Every per-image mutation route authorizes and then writes as two separate statements, so a permission that is revoked in between is applied anyway:

```python
_assert_image_owner(image_name, current_user)          # decision
ApiDependencies.invoker.services.images.update(...)    # write, under a decision that may be stale
```

The window is small but it is a real check-then-act: between the two statements a board can flip from Public to Private, an image can be reassigned to a board the caller cannot write to, or the caller's access to the board can be withdrawn. The write still lands.

### What is already conditional

#9394 closed the one instance where the race caused *incorrect data movement* rather than merely a late-by-microseconds mutation. `board_image_records.remove_image_from_board` scopes its DELETE to the board the caller was authorized against:

```sql
DELETE FROM board_images WHERE image_name = ? AND board_id = ?;
```

An unscoped delete followed the image if it moved between the authorization and the write, applying a decision taken about one board to a different one. The scoped form matches zero rows instead, and the route classifies the zero-row outcome (moved / already uncategorized / deleted) rather than reporting a success that did not happen.

The remaining routes — star, unstar, add-to-board — have no equivalent. Their worst case is a mutation applied under a decision that was true a moment earlier, which is why this is a follow-up and not a blocker on that PR.

### Why the obvious fix does not fit

Encoding the authorization as a WHERE clause means encoding *all* of it, and it is a four-way disjunction spanning three tables (`invokeai/app/api/routers/_access.py`):

- the caller is an admin (`users.is_admin`), or
- the caller owns the image (`images.user_id`), or
- the caller owns the board the image sits on (`board_images` → `boards.user_id`), or
- that board is Public (`boards.board_visibility`).

Writing that as a correlated subquery on every mutating statement duplicates the policy in SQL, in several places, with no mechanism keeping the copies in step with the Python one. The first divergence is a silent authorization bug.

### The shape that would work

Move the decision *into* the service call, so authorization and mutation share one transaction and one policy implementation:

- a single `authorize_image_mutation(image_name, user)` used by the service layer inside the transaction that performs the write, rather than by each route beforehand;
- routes keep reporting per-name outcomes exactly as they do now (`failed_images` for a genuine failure, silent skip for a name the caller may not touch), so the API contract does not change;
- storage errors keep propagating rather than being read as "denied" (the invariant #9394 established).

This is the same refactor already wanted for the last-admin guards, which have the identical check-then-act shape in `UserService`. Worth doing once, for both.

### Not urgent because

- The mutations at risk (star, unstar, board add) are low-impact and visible to the user who performed them.
- The high-impact case — a delete or a board move landing on the wrong board — is already conditional.
- Any fix touches the service interfaces for images, boards and users together, which is a poor fit for a bug-fix PR.

items.title: k8s-event-watcher: the #1351 forbidden hold is gated on never-synced, so a permission revoked across a running fleet still retries indefinitely
items.body:
**Kind:** Bug

Filed against #1351 (open), not against `main`. The hold that PR adds is the right shape; this is about the case it deliberately leaves on the default backoff, and why that case is the more likely way a fleet arrives at #1333.

## The gate

`handleWatchError` holds only when the reflector has never completed a list:

```go
synced := r != nil && r.LastSyncResourceVersion() != ""
if !apierrors.IsForbidden(err) || synced {
    cache.DefaultWatchErrorHandler(ctx, r, err)
    return
}
```

The stated reason is sound as far as it goes: once a cluster has synced, `cluster_up` reads `1`, nothing inside the informer can lower it, and holding there would report a cluster as watched while its events go up to ten minutes stale.

## Why that leaves the bug reachable

#1333's fleet reaches the refused state at *startup* — the identity never had `container.events.list`. That is one of two ways to get there, and the other is the one an operating fleet is more likely to hit: a binding edited, an IAM role removed, a Config Connector or Terraform apply that narrows a custom role, an org policy rollout. In every one of those the clusters have already synced. The 403 arrives from the watch, `synced` is true, and each cluster relists on the default backoff — the same 30-to-60-second-per-cluster churn, times 26, logged twice per attempt, for the life of the process. That is exactly the state the reporter's container OOMKilled in.

So after #1351 the watcher holds for the cold-start shape of the problem and not for the revocation shape, even though the fix's own doc comment names revocation as a case it routes to the default handler. A fleet that loses the permission at 03:00 on a Tuesday is back to #1333, and the `GOMEMLIMIT` guard in the same PR is then the only thing between it and the OOM loop — a soft limit, which makes GC aggressive but does not cap live heap.

## The metric objection has a cheap answer

"Cannot be lowered from inside the informer" is true of the current structure, not a constraint of the design. `Run` already takes a callback for exactly this purpose, and `main.go` already owns the gauge in a closure beside it:

```go
onSynced := func() {
    synced.Add(1)
    m.clusterUp.WithLabelValues(tc.Name, tc.ProjectID, tc.Location).Set(1)
    ...
}
```

A sibling `onDegraded func()` (or a single `onWatching func(bool)`) lets the handler hold a post-sync 403 *and* keep `cluster_up` honest by setting it to `0` first — which is arguably more honest than today, where a cluster whose watch is being refused every 30 seconds keeps reporting `1` until the process ends. `cluster_up`'s documented meaning ("`1` means events are genuinely flowing") is already not what a post-sync 403 loop produces.

That also removes the asymmetry where the same denial gets two different treatments depending on whether it arrived before or after the first successful list, which is a distinction the cluster operator did not make and cannot see.

## Suggested change

Drop the `synced` gate from the hold, and add the callback so `cluster_up` drops to `0` for the held cluster and returns to `1` when a later attempt succeeds. The identity-with-`list`-but-not-`watch` case that the gate also catches is served by the same treatment: it is a permission problem, it does not resolve on a connection's clock, and ten minutes of staleness reported as `cluster_up=0` beats one minute of staleness reported as `cluster_up=1`.

If the ten-minute hold feels too long for a cluster that *was* working, a shorter post-sync hold (a minute, say) would still collapse the churn by an order of magnitude and keep the fix's cold-start behaviour untouched.

## Related

Separately filed: a `SelfSubjectAccessReview` preflight before each informer is created, which addresses the startup half without any retry loop at all. The two are complementary — a preflight cannot see a permission revoked later, and the hold is what covers that.

items.title: fix: revoked permissions still resolve as authorized
items.body:
`verifyPermission` in `src/resolver/didValidator.ts` checks a perm's `type` and effective window but never `revoked`, so a revoked perm keeps resolving `authorized: true` until its `effective_until`.
Seen on `testnet`: revoked an issuer perm, 40 min later `issuer-authorization` still returns `authorized: true`, even though the indexer returns that perm with `revoked` set.

items.title: [bug-fix] Permission revoked approver can still perform workflow approval tasks
items.body:
## Purpose
Update pending approval task corresponding to the workflow, when the flow is updated.

## Approach
For each `pending` state request under the changed workflow, check whether the workflow changes have affected the current  state of the request. If affected:
- `READY` state requests are removed and recreated according to new workflow configs.
-  `RESERVED` / `BLOCKED` state requests are checked for the eligibility to have the same state under the new configs. And if yes; a new set of tasks with  `RESERVED` / `BLOCKED` is created or else a new `READY` state is created.

items.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Environment

```markdown
- Milvus version: 2.6.4-20251019-82c019181-f1f3252
- Deployment mode(standalone or cluster): both 
- MQ type(rocksmq, pulsar or kafka): both    
- SDK version(e.g. pymilvus v2.0.0rc2): 2.7.0rc25
- OS(Ubuntu or CentOS): 
- CPU/Memory: 
- GPU: 
- Others:
```

### Current Behavior

1.  do mix action(insert/search/delete)
2.  kms:Decrypt permission of the KMS Key is revoked
3. fail to insert/delete, but search still success (because data has already been loaded into memory)

### Expected Behavior

After kms:Decrypt permission of the KMS Key is revoked,  search failed or was successful but the reason for success must be informed: it is because the data has been loaded into memory and is no longer under the control of kms.

### Steps To Reproduce

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Final version of Milvus mixed business concurrency test script
Simplified version for stable operation
"""

import threading
import time
import random
import logging
from pymilvus import MilvusClient, DataType, CollectionSchema, FieldSchema

# ================= Configuration =================
MILVUS_URI = ("https://in01-f36afbf23054443.aws-us-west-2.vectordb-uat3.zillizcloud.com:19532")
TOKEN = "root:S6+L!7Y3Eoh2@<DvePCqzex}3O(R7jhU"
DATABASE = "cmek_database_rN8cFfV7"
# DATABASE = "default"
COLLECTION_NAME = "old_mixed_test"
DIM = 768

# ================= Logging Configuration =================
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s',
    handlers=[
        logging.StreamHandler(),  # 输出到标准输出
        logging.FileHandler('milvus_test.log')  # 同时输出到文件
    ]
)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Business pressure configuration (number of requests per operation type)
# BUSINESS_CONFIG = {
#     "insert": 200000,   # Number of insert operations
#     "upsert": 10000,    # Number of upsert operations
#     "delete": 10000,    # Number of delete operations
#     "search": 100000,    # Number of search operations
# }
BUSINESS_CONFIG = {
    "insert": 1000,   # Number of insert operations
    "upsert": 1000,    # Number of upsert operations
    "delete": 1000,    # Number of delete operations
    "search": 1000,    # Number of search operations
}

# Global statistics results
results = {
    "insert": {"success": 0, "fail": 0, "times": [], "errors": []},
    "upsert": {"success": 0, "fail": 0, "times": [], "errors": []},
    "delete": {"success": 0, "fail": 0, "times": [], "errors": []},
    "search": {"success": 0, "fail": 0, "times": [], "errors": []},
}
results_lock = threading.Lock()

# Monitoring flag
monitoring = True

# ================= Utility Functions =================
def random_vector(count=1):
    """Generate random vector"""
    data = []
    if count == 1:
        return [random.random() for _ in range(DIM)]
    for i in range(count):
        data.append([random.random() for _ in range(DIM)])
    return data

def random_data(count=1):
    """Generate random test data"""
    data = []
    for i in range(count):
        data.append({
            "embedding": random_vector(1),
            "text": f"text_{random.randint(1, 10000)}",
            "category": random.randint(1, 100000),
            "score": random.random()
        })
    return data

def record_result(operation, success, response_time, error_message=None):
    """Record operation result"""
    with results_lock:
        results[operation]["success" if success else "fail"] += 1
        results[operation]["times"].append(response_time)
        if not success and error_message:
            results[operation]["errors"].append(error_message)

# ================= Business Operation Functions =================
def insert_worker():
    """Insert operation worker thread"""
    logger.info(f"Starting insert operations, target requests: "
                f"{BUSINESS_CONFIG['insert']}")

    for i in range(BUSINESS_CONFIG['insert']):
        start_time = time.time()
        try:
            data = random_data(200)
            # Remove id field since collection has auto_id=True
            # if "id" in data[0]:
            #     del data[0]["id"]

            result = client.insert(collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME, data=data)
            response_time = time.time() - start_time

            if result.get('insert_count', 0) > 0:
                record_result("insert", True, response_time)
            else:
                error_msg = f"Insert failed: {result}"
                record_result("insert", False, response_time, error_msg)
                logger.error(error_msg)

        except Exception as e:
            response_time = time.time() - start_time
            error_msg = f"Insert error: {e}"
            record_result("insert", False, response_time, error_msg)
            logger.error(error_msg)

        # Control request frequency
        # time.sleep(0.001)

def upsert_worker():
    """Upsert operation worker thread"""
    logger.info(f"Starting upsert operations, target requests: "
                f"{BUSINESS_CONFIG['upsert']}")

    # First insert some data for upsert
    logger.info("Inserting some data for upsert...")
    initial_data = random_data(100)  # Insert 10 records
    try:
        insert_result = client.insert(collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME, data=initial_data)
        inserted_ids = insert_result.get('ids', [])
        logger.info(f"Inserted {len(inserted_ids)} records for upsert")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Initial insert failed: {e}")
        inserted_ids = []

    for i in range(BUSINESS_CONFIG['upsert']):
        start_time = time.time()
        try:
            data = random_data(1)
            # Use existing ID for upsert
            if inserted_ids:
                data[0]["id"] = inserted_ids[i % len(inserted_ids)]

            result = client.upsert(collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME, data=data)
            response_time = time.time() - start_time

            if result.get('upsert_count', 0) > 0:
                record_result("upsert", True, response_time)
            else:
                error_msg = f"Upsert failed: {result}"
                record_result("upsert", False, response_time, error_msg)
                logger.error(error_msg)

        except Exception as e:
            response_time = time.time() - start_time
            error_msg = f"Upsert error: {e}"
            record_result("upsert", False, response_time, error_msg)
            logger.error(error_msg)

        time.sleep(0.2)

def delete_worker():
    """Delete operation worker thread"""
    logger.info(f"Starting delete operations, target requests: "
                f"{BUSINESS_CONFIG['delete']}")

    for i in range(BUSINESS_CONFIG['delete']):
        start_time = time.time()
        try:
            # Randomly delete data of a certain category
            category = random.randint(1, 10)
            filter_expr = f"category == {category}"

            client.delete(collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME, filter=filter_expr)
            response_time = time.time() - start_time

            record_result("delete", True, response_time)

        except Exception as e:
            response_time = time.time() - start_time
            error_msg = f"Delete error: {e}"
            record_result("delete", False, response_time, error_msg)
            logger.error(error_msg)

        time.sleep(0.3)

def search_worker():
    """Search operation worker thread"""
    logger.info(f"Starting search operations, target requests: "
                f"{BUSINESS_CONFIG['search']}")

    for i in range(BUSINESS_CONFIG['search']):
        start_time = time.time()
        try:
            search_vector = random_vector(10)

            # Randomly decide whether to use filter conditions
            use_filter = random.random() < 0.3
            filter_expr = (f"category == {random.randint(1, 1000)}"
                           if use_filter else None)

            result = client.search(
                collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME,
                data=search_vector,
                anns_field="embedding",
                search_params={"metric_type": "L2", "params": {"nprobe": 10}},
                output_fields=["id", "embedding"],
                limit=100,
                filter=filter_expr
            )

            response_time = time.time() - start_time

            if result and len(result) > 0:
                record_result("search", True, response_time)
            else:
                error_msg = "Search failed: no results"
                record_result("search", False, response_time, error_msg)

        except Exception as e:
            response_time = time.time() - start_time
            error_msg = f"Search error: {e}"
            record_result("search", False, response_time, error_msg)
            logger.error(error_msg)

        # time.sleep(0.002)

def monitor_progress():
    """Monitor progress, log statistics every 60 seconds"""
    global monitoring
    while monitoring:
        time.sleep(30)  # Wait 60 seconds

        if not monitoring:
            break

        with results_lock:
            logger.info("\n" + "="*60)
            logger.info(f"📊 Real-time Monitoring Report - "
                        f"{time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
            logger.info("="*60)

            total_requests = 0
            total_success = 0
            total_fail = 0

            for operation, stats in results.items():
                success = stats["success"]
                fail = stats["fail"]
                total = success + fail
                total_requests += total
                total_success += success
                total_fail += fail

                if total > 0:
                    success_rate = success / total
                    fail_rate = fail / total
                    avg_time = (sum(stats["times"]) / len(stats["times"])
                                if stats["times"] else 0)

                    logger.info(f"\n🔹 {operation.upper()}:")
                    logger.info(f"   Total requests: {total}")
                    logger.info(f"   Success: {success} ({success_rate:.2%})")
                    logger.info(f"   Failed: {fail} ({fail_rate:.2%})")
                    logger.info(f"   Average response time: {avg_time:.3f}s")

                    # Show recent errors
                    if stats["errors"]:
                        recent_errors = stats["errors"][-3:]  # Show last 3 errors
                        logger.info("   Recent errors:")
                        for error in recent_errors:
                            logger.info(f"     - {error}")

            # Overall statistics
            if total_requests > 0:
                overall_success_rate = total_success / total_requests
                overall_fail_rate = total_fail / total_requests
                logger.info(f"\n📈 Overall Statistics:")
                logger.info(f"   Total requests: {total_requests}")
                logger.info(f"   Total success: {total_success} ({overall_success_rate:.2%})")
                logger.info(f"   Total failed: {total_fail} ({overall_fail_rate:.2%})")

            logger.info("="*60)

# ================= Main Function =================
def main():
    global client

    logger.info("=== Milvus Mixed Business Concurrency Test ===")


    # Connect to Milvus
    logger.info("Connecting to Milvus...")
    client = MilvusClient(uri=MILVUS_URI, token=TOKEN)
    client.using_database(DATABASE)

    # Delete existing collection (if exists)
    if client.has_collection(COLLECTION_NAME):
        logger.info(f"Deleting existing collection: {COLLECTION_NAME}")
        client.drop_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)

    # Create collection
    logger.info(f"Creating collection: {COLLECTION_NAME}")
    # fields = [
    #     FieldSchema(name="id", dtype=DataType.INT64, is_primary=True, auto_id=True),
    #     FieldSchema(name="embedding", dtype=DataType.FLOAT_VECTOR, dim=DIM, mmap_enabled=True),
    #     FieldSchema(name="text", dtype=DataType.VARCHAR, max_length=1000, is_clustering_key=True, mmap_enabled=True),
    #     FieldSchema(name="category", dtype=DataType.INT64, default_value=100, is_partition_key=True, mmap_enabled=True),
    #     FieldSchema(name="score", dtype=DataType.FLOAT, nullable=True)
    # ]
    fields = [
        FieldSchema(name="id", dtype=DataType.INT64, is_primary=True, auto_id=True),
        FieldSchema(name="embedding", dtype=DataType.FLOAT_VECTOR, dim=DIM),
        FieldSchema(name="text", dtype=DataType.VARCHAR, max_length=1000, is_clustering_key=True),
        FieldSchema(name="category", dtype=DataType.INT64),
        FieldSchema(name="score", dtype=DataType.FLOAT)
    ]
    schema = CollectionSchema(fields=fields)
    client.create_collection(collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME, schema=schema)

    # Create index
    logger.info("Creating index...")
    from pymilvus.milvus_client.index import IndexParams
    index_params = IndexParams()
    index_params.add_index(
        field_name="embedding",
        index_type="HNSW",
        metric_type="L2",
        params={"nlist": 1024}
    )
    client.create_index(
        collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME,
        index_params=index_params
    )

    # Load collection
    logger.info("Loading collection...")
    client.load_collection(COLLECTION_NAME)

    # Wait for loading to complete
    logger.info("Waiting for collection loading to complete...")
    time.sleep(3)

    # Check loading state
    load_state = client.get_load_state(COLLECTION_NAME)
    logger.info(f"Collection loading state: {load_state}")

    # Start concurrent testing
    logger.info("\nStarting concurrent testing...")
    start_time = time.time()

    # Create and start monitoring thread
    monitor_thread = threading.Thread(target=monitor_progress, daemon=True)
    monitor_thread.start()

    # Create and start business threads
    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=insert_worker),
        threading.Thread(target=upsert_worker),
        threading.Thread(target=delete_worker),
        threading.Thread(target=search_worker),
    ]

    for t in threads:
        t.start()

    # Wait for all business threads to complete
    for t in threads:
        t.join()

    # Stop monitoring
    global monitoring
    monitoring = False

    end_time = time.time()
    duration = end_time - start_time

    # Log results
    logger.info("\n=== Test Results ===")
    logger.info(f"Total test duration: {duration:.2f} seconds")
    logger.info("-" * 50)

    total_requests = 0
    total_success = 0

    for operation, stats in results.items():
        success = stats["success"]
        fail = stats["fail"]
        total = success + fail
        total_requests += total
        total_success += success

        if total > 0:
            success_rate = success / total
            avg_time = sum(stats["times"]) / len(stats["times"]) if stats["times"] else 0
            rps = total / duration

            logger.info(f"{operation.upper()}:")
            logger.info(f"  Total requests: {total}")
            logger.info(f"  Success: {success}")
            logger.info(f"  Failed: {fail}")
            logger.info(f"  Success rate: {success_rate:.2%}")
            logger.info(f"  Average response time: {avg_time:.3f}s")
            logger.info(f"  Requests per second: {rps:.2f}")
            logger.info("")

    # Overall statistics
    overall_success_rate = total_success / total_requests if total_requests > 0 else 0
    overall_rps = total_requests / duration

    logger.info("Overall Statistics:")
    logger.info(f"  Total requests: {total_requests}")
    logger.info(f"  Total success: {total_success}")
    logger.info(f"  Total failed: {total_requests - total_success}")
    logger.info(f"  Overall success rate: {overall_success_rate:.2%}")
    logger.info(f"  Overall error rate: {1-overall_success_rate:.2%}")
    logger.info(f"  Overall QPS: {overall_rps:.2f}")

    res = client.compact(collection_name=COLLECTION_NAME, is_clustering=True)
    logger.info(f"Compact result: {res}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

items.title: Permission revoked approver can still perform workflow approval tasks
items.body:
### Description

When an approval request is sent for multiple users, and then the approval steps are updated to revoke the approver permissions, still the approval requests are listed and the revoked approver can approve, reject or claim the approval request. It get's risky when the permission revoked approver claims it for himself, resulting on others being blocked to perform any actions for that request.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cb8a52e-57d4-40de-96e8-8fe8dd6b3d1a

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Login as super admin user
2. Create an additional admin user and add console administrator role
3. Create a workflow for user creation.
4. Add approval step for Administrator role.
5. Create a new user. Approval will be available for both admin users.
6. Update the approval workflow to have only the super admin in the approval step.
7. Login as the created admin user.
8. Notice that the user creation request is still visible for the created admin and have the option to perform approval functions.
9. Click on claim which reserves the request for the created admin.
10. Now any other users that created admin shouldn't be able to perform approval actions since the state is BLOCKED

### Please select the area issue is related to

User & Identity Administration

items.title: [0.25, new ACL/RBAC] User still has the access if permissions are revoked in config and user didn't logged out.
items.body:
Playing with new ACLs. Using roles topic-reader & topic-writer from supplied config example. 
Assigned some user (tested with basic-auth) both roles on one cluster. Good so far. Can read/write/modify topics in that cluster. Then I remove topic-writer in the config for that user, leaving only topic-reader. Restart AKHQ, but user was still logged on. Once AKHQ restarts, user was still able to create a new topic in that cluster in the UI. New permissions take effect after I logout & login back again with that user. At least "Create topic" button are gone and create topic URL which previously show a form to type a topic name, etc now just tries to view non-existing topic "create" iirc.
I don't have any knowledge on how permissions are implemented internally, but how that's possible? Just a guess, that either permissions get cached somehow or even worse - stored client side and trusted without checks? Or am I just missing something important and misconfigured?

```yaml
...
akhq:
  security:
    roles:
      topic-reader:
        - resources: [ "TOPIC", "TOPIC_DATA" ]
          actions: [ "READ" ]
        - resources: [ "TOPIC" ]
          actions: [ "READ_CONFIG" ]
      topic-writer:
        - resources: [ "TOPIC", "TOPIC_DATA" ]
          actions: [ "CREATE", "UPDATE" ]
        - resources: [ "TOPIC" ]
          actions: [ "ALTER_CONFIG" ]

    groups:
      custom-group:
        - role: topic-reader
          clusters: [ "some-test-cluster" ]
        - role: topic-writer # that line will be removed
          clusters: [ "some-test-cluster" ] and that line removed as well

    basic-auth:
      - username: testuser
        password: "<password hash>"
        groups:
          - custom-group
...
```
